subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What scope should maintainers accept for this broad native VPS reasoning-latency investigation?
rationale: The repository has partial diagnostics and docs, but turning a user-specific performance analysis into maintainable work requires a human choice of measurement environment, acceptance criteria, and whether the output should be docs-only or include new instrumentation.

options.title: Scope a measured runbook
options.body: Publish or assign a bounded native-Linux runbook that uses existing diagnostics first and opens follow-up PRs only for proven missing spans or hot paths.

options.title: Split into narrower subsystem issues
options.body: Convert the request into separate context, memory, compaction, Telegram, and gateway scheduling issues before any implementation work starts.

options.title: Treat as support only
options.body: Close the core tracking item after pointing the reporter to existing tuning docs and ask for a new issue with repeatable traces if a specific bottleneck remains.

recommendation.title: Scope a measured runbook
recommendation.body: Publish or assign a bounded native-Linux runbook that uses existing diagnostics first and opens follow-up PRs only for proven missing spans or hot paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to steipete as the strongest cross-cutting docs and observability owner for deciding whether this becomes a runbook, docs update, or deeper instrumentation effort.
